title: Apostate canonical launch configuration
description: The normalized launch contract shared by the CLI, Python package, and Node package. Profile selection precedence is explicit profile file > explicit profile ID > fingerprint seed plus platform persona > platform default > host inheritance. Network localization precedence is explicit locale/timezone > GeoIP-derived locale/timezone > profile-selected locale/timezone > host values. A launch resolves this configuration once before the browser process starts; adapters must not add per-call randomness and must not log proxy credentials.

fingerprint.description: A deterministic profile selector. It may be a non-negative integer or a non-empty stable seed string. Null leaves selection to the next available precedence source. Integer seeds are bounded to remain exact in JavaScript and JSON number implementations; string seeds are normalized as opaque identifiers and must not contain credentials or whitespace.

fingerprint_platform.description: The platform persona used with fingerprint. Null permits platform default or host inheritance. This is a persona name, not the release artifact target; release targets are recorded in release/manifest.schema.json.

profile.description: An explicit profile file path, profile ID, or inline device-profile object. A non-null value takes precedence over fingerprint selection. Inline objects must validate against the public device-profile schema.

locale.description: An explicit BCP 47 locale tag. When non-null it wins over GeoIP and profile locale selection; null allows the network/profile/host precedence chain.

timezone.description: An explicit IANA-style timezone name (or UTC/GMT). When non-null it wins over GeoIP and profile timezone selection; null allows the network/profile/host precedence chain.

geoip.description: Resolve the observed network exit before launch and use its location for locale/timezone only when those values were not explicitly supplied. A failed lookup must be reported rather than silently inventing values.

proxy.description: An opaque HTTP(S), SOCKS4, or SOCKS5 proxy URI. Userinfo is accepted for authenticated proxies and must be kept in memory only: adapters and diagnostics must redact it and must never emit it in logs or manifests.

headless.description: Whether to start Chromium in headless mode.

user_data_dir.description: Persistent user-data directory path. Null requests an adapter-managed temporary profile.

args.description: Additional Chromium command-line arguments. Arguments are opaque to this contract; adapters must avoid logging values that can contain proxy credentials or other secrets.
